links.outcome: Radiologist recall decisions and confidence when FDR/FOR shown alongside AI scores versus scores alone
links.effect: Recall was higher with AI scores alone than with FDR/FOR (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.331-6.417, p=0.0077); confidence was higher when FDR/FOR were provided, especially at intermediate scores.
links.quote: Confidence followed a U-shaped relationship with score and was higher when FDR/FOR were provided, particularly at intermediate scores.

links.outcome: Locally calibrated FDR and FOR estimated per score threshold from local retrospective mammograms
links.effect: FDR and FOR varied from 60.87% and 0.03% at low scores to 99.26% and 0.65% at high scores across 130,712 mammograms.
links.quote: FDR and FOR varied substantially across AI score thresholds, ranging from 60.87% and 0.03%, respectively, at the low end of the score distribution to 99.26%% and 0.65% at the high end.

links.effect: AI scores alone had higher recall than FDR/FOR: OR 2.9, 95% CI [1.331, 6.417], p=0.0077.
links.quote: In the decision-making study (n=21; 20 assessments per radiologist), recall increased with AI score in both conditions; however, recall was higher when AI scores were presented alone compared with scores accompanied by FDR/FOR (odds ratio 2.9, 95% CI [1.331, 6.417], p=0.0077).
